Changed `/worktree/local_day.py` only (read-only `test_local_day.py` untouched):

- `phoenix_day()`: subtracts fixed 7h (Phoenix is UTC-7, no DST) from the epoch-ms instant via naive `datetime` + `timedelta` arithmetic, then formats the date — no `zoneinfo`/tz database used.
- Added `day_bounds_ms(day)`: parses `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, computes midnight Phoenix = 07:00 UTC via `calendar.timegm` (exact integer ms, host-tz independent), returns `(start_ms, start_ms + 86400000)`.

```

OK
```

2. `cd /worktree && python3 -c "from local_day import phoenix_day, day_bounds_ms ..."` (evening/bounds/zoneinfo check)
```
2026-09-25
1790319600000 1790406000000 86400000
2026-09-25 2026-09-24 2026-09-26
False False
```
Evening case (2026-09-26 02:00 UTC = 19:00 Phoenix 09-25) now returns `2026-09-25`; bounds round-trip: `start->09-25`, `start-1ms->09-24`, `end->09-26`; no `zoneinfo`/`tzdata` references.

meta.finalPromptText:
local_day.phoenix_day() returns the UTC calendar date, so evening timestamps land on the
next day. Phoenix is UTC-7 all year (no daylight saving). Fix phoenix_day() without
depending on the zoneinfo/tz database (it is not installed in every runtime), and add
day_bounds_ms(day) that takes "YYYY-MM-DD" and returns (start_ms, end_ms): epoch
milliseconds of the start of that Phoenix calendar day and of the next day's start (end
exclusive).
